title: Improvement of montmorillonite adsorption capacity for lead ions by modifying with hexadecyl trimethyl ammonium chloride: Characterization, modelling and optimization studies
author: Massoudinejad, Mohseni, et al.

steps.title: Prepare modified nanoclay adsorbent
steps.instruction: Synthesize four batches of montmorillonite nanoclay modified with hexadecyl trimethyl ammonium chloride (HTAC) at different surfactant concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Add the desired concentration of HTAC surfactant to separate 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks (one flask per concentration).
Add 3 g of Cloisite Na+ nanoclay (montmorillonite) to each flask.
Stir the suspensions on a shaker for 1 day (≈24 h) at 20 °C, 300 rpm, and pH 7.0.
Centrifuge each suspension (centrifugation parameters not specified) to collect the solid.
Wash the collected solids five times with deionized water.
Dry the washed solids in an oven at 105 °C until completely dry.
Store the dried, modified nanoclay adsorbents in sealed polyethylene bottles.

steps.title: Characterize modified adsorbent
steps.instruction: Analyze the physical and structural properties of the HTAC‑modified montmorillonite.

substeps.instruction: Observe surface morphology with Field‑Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM) coupled to Energy Dispersive X‑ray analysis (EDAX) at 15 kV, using background subtraction with 240 scans and a scanning speed of 0.02 s⁻¹.
Calculate the interlayer d‑spacing from the FESEM data using Bragg’s equation (nλ = 2d sin θ).
Record powder X‑ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns using Cu Kα radiation (λ = 1.54 Å) over a 2θ range of 10–120°, with a scan speed of 1 s per step at 25 °C.
Determine specific surface area and pore‑size distribution by applying the Brunauer‑Emmett‑Teller (BET) method and the Barrett‑Joyner‑Halenda (BJH) analysis, respectively.

steps.title: Perform Pb2+ adsorption experiments
steps.instruction: Evaluate lead‑ion removal by the modified nanoclay under controlled conditions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1000 mg L⁻¹ Pb²⁺ stock solution using Pb²⁺ salt from Merck.
Dilute the stock solution to the required test concentrations using the relation C₁V₁ = C₂V₂.
In a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask, add 100 mL of the diluted Pb²⁺ solution for each experiment.
Adjust the solution pH to the desired value with acid or base.
Add the predetermined dose of HTAC‑modified nanoclay adsorbent (and any additional surfactant if required) to the flask.
Mix the suspension for the specified contact time (duration as defined in the experimental design).
Centrifuge the mixture for 5 min at 5000 rpm to separate the solid adsorbent.
Measure the residual Pb²⁺ concentration in the supernatant using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP‑OES).
